title: Dragging a layer feels physical: the row lifts, rides the pointer up and down, and the list opens a gap for it
goal: User 2026-09-30: 'when I try to rearrange layers, the drag is not smooth. I want to drag the item intuitively and have something of a shadow where it will be dropped that gets injected in the spot, and things make room for it. It should feel super smooth and not like you're dragging some random thing and hoping for an insertion line to show up, but things move out of the way for you and you're dragging the item and it is horizontally locked but you can vertically move it up and down the list. If you drag a group, we minimize it and let you drag the root and position it elsewhere... if you drag to the end of a group, does it land inside the group or below the group? I think we can solve that by which item's half you're over. If you're over the bottom half of the group's last item, into group. If top half of item below, inserted below group.' Applies to the Layers list in the right panel (and the timeline's track headers where tracks reorder). Replaces today's drag-image plus insertion line. Reference: docs/design/mocks/pages/layers-pane.html; UX-PATTERNS motion rules for a list that only moves.
acceptance: Drop rules in PhotonzCore first, with tests, exactly as the user specified: the target is decided by which half of which row the pointer is over; over the bottom half of a group's LAST child lands inside the group as its last child; over the top half of the row below the group lands below the group at the group's level; top half of a row inserts above it, bottom half below it (and into an expanded group's first slot when over the bottom half of the group header); a group can never be dropped into itself or its descendants; locked layers and the canvas/background row keep their rules
Pressing and moving a row lifts it: the real row (not a ghosted drag image) rises with a soft shadow and slight scale, follows the pointer vertically 1:1, and is locked horizontally

The other rows move out of the way with a smooth spring as the pointer crosses row halves, opening a gap exactly the dragged row's height where it will land (the 'shadow' slot), so the drop place is always visible without an insertion line
Dragging a group collapses it into its header row for the drag (children tucked away with a quick animation) and restores its expansion after the drop
Letting go settles the row into the gap with the same spring; Esc returns it to where it came from; the whole move is one undo step
Near the list's top or bottom edge the list autoscrolls smoothly, and the gap keeps tracking the pointer
60 fps throughout with 200 layers (Instruments or a signpost walk); no row jumps or flickers

Walk at Next defaults with pointer drags: reorder within a list, into the end of a group (bottom half of its last child), out below a group (top half of the row below), drag a group elsewhere; photograph mid-drag (lifted row, open gap) and after

log.note: Pre-build review: today's reorder is a system drag (onDrag + NSItemProvider, a ghost image) plus a 2pt drop line, read in thirds (LayerDropZone). New plan: a pointer gesture on the list itself (not per row, so a lazily unbuilt row can never cancel it), a pure LayerRowDrag model in PhotonzCore that reads HALVES against the list as drawn (gap included, which is what gives natural hysteresis), and a real LayersRow drawn lifted over the stack while its slot becomes a shadow gap indented to the landing depth. Risks found: (1) the mock's point 4 lets you drop INTO a shut group by hovering it; halves alone lose that, so a shut group springs open after a short rest (the mock's own second half) and then its bottom half means first slot. (2) SwiftUI only runs a DragGesture in the active app, so a pointer walk needs the Mac to itself; the lock-safe dragRow step is rewired to drive the same session the gesture drives. (3) The layers list is shared with Current, so the new drag sits behind a Next flag on by default in Next; Current keeps the drop line. (4) Timeline track headers are left for a follow-up: the acceptance list is all about the Layers list.
owns these walks: layer-row-lifts-walk, layer-row-lifts-by-pointer-walk, layer-row-lifts-at-scale-walk

Built: PhotonzCore/LayerRowDrag.swift (halves read against the list as drawn, gap + depth, offsets, spring target, reflow, returnHome; 24 tests in LayerRowDragTests). App: LayerRowDragSession (on EditorState, so walks drive the same drag), LayerRowDragViews (placement, gap, lifted row, count badge, AppKit scroll for edge autoscroll), LayersListView wiring behind next-a-dragged-layer-lifts (on in Next only). Walks: layer-row-lifts-walk (scripted, 9 drags incl. Escape, spring-open, multi-row, light mode, undo), layer-row-lifts-by-pointer-walk (posted mouse events through the list's own gesture; needs the Mac), layer-row-lifts-at-scale-walk (173 layers, carry longest pass 8.6ms). New walk step expectRows; dragRow gained cancel.

Gotchas found by reproduction: (1) removing the row's onDrag took away click-through, so the FIRST click on a row of a window in the back (the Twist, in every walk that presses it) only brought the window forward; fixed with .allowsWindowActivationEvents on the list (verified: Twist opens with the probe in the back). (2) Edge autoscroll through SwiftUI ScrollPosition rebuilt the whole list every tick (15 list bodies for one carry, longest pass 17ms at 173 rows); now scrolls the enclosing NSScrollView directly (8 list bodies, one per row passed, longest 8.6ms). (3) After a swap the pointer sits in the gap, so 'resting on a shut group' has to include resting in the gap right under it (LayerRowDrag.springTarget).

left rough: the drop's own main-thread pass is 37-49ms at 173 layers (document edit + list + canvas), after the settle so nothing is moving; spring-open costs ~30ms like the twist does. Neither earned a task: no motion is on screen at that moment. row-put-down-walk still proves the old system-drag cleanup (LayerRowInHand), which only Current uses now; left as is since that code still ships in Current. A pointer drag's trailing tap on the row was not checked with a multi-selection. Rough items in the audit: timeline track headers filed as timeline-tracks-reorder-by-dragging-their-header; the rest stay here.

Shipped in Next (flag next-a-dragged-layer-lifts, on by default): a dragged layer row lifts and rides the pointer vertically, the rows spring aside and the gap (indented to its landing depth) is the drop place; halves rule incl. group foot vs row below, group travels shut and reopens, multi-row carries as one with a count, shut group springs open on rest, Escape returns, one undo step, edge autoscroll. Core rules in PhotonzCore/LayerRowDrag.swift with 24 tests; full suite 10,736 green. Verified by layer-row-lifts-walk (9 scripted drags with expectRows after each, mid-drag pictures, light mode, undo), layer-row-lifts-by-pointer-walk (real posted mouse drags through the gesture) and layer-row-lifts-at-scale-walk (173 layers, carry peak 8.6ms/pass); 29 neighbouring layers-list walks green.
